hero.title: Vaporetto Meaning
hero.description: A vaporetto is a motorboat serving as a canal bus in Venice, Italy — the city's primary form of public transport through its historic canals and lagoon. The word comes from Italian vapore (steam) plus the diminutive suffix -etto, literally meaning little steamer, named for the steam-powered boats that first served Venice in the 19th century. Today, the vaporetto network connects the historic centre, the lagoon islands and the mainland, carrying millions of residents and visitors each year. This guide covers the word's meaning, its history, the routes and lines, tickets and prices, and how to ride Venice's waterbus system.

aboutGame.title: What Does Vaporetto Mean?
paragraphs: The vaporetto meaning is straightforward and beautiful at once: a motorboat serving as a canal bus in Venice, Italy. The word itself is a small piece of linguistic history — from Italian vapore meaning steam or steamboat, combined with the diminutive suffix -etto, producing vaporetto: literally, a little steamer. The name was earned honestly: the first vaporetti that navigated Venice's Grand Canal in the late 19th century were indeed steam-powered, and though today's fleet runs on diesel and increasingly electric motors, the name has stayed as an artifact of the technology that started it all.

The plural is vaporetti, and the word functions as both a noun and a brand — ACTV, Venice's public transport company, operates the official vaporetto network of more than twenty lines connecting the historic centre, the lagoon islands (Murano, Burano, Lido, San Giorgio), and the mainland via Punta Sabbioni and Fusina. The vaporetto is not a tourist attraction though tourists ride it; it is Venice's bus, metro and commute, carrying residents to work and visitors to St Mark's Square with equal efficiency. Understanding the vaporetto meaning is understanding Venice itself: a city where the bus floats.

items.question: What does vaporetto mean?
items.answer: A vaporetto is a motorboat serving as a canal bus in Venice, Italy. The word comes from Italian vapore (steam) plus the diminutive suffix -etto, literally meaning little steamer. The plural is vaporetti.

items.question: How much does a vaporetto ticket cost?
items.answer: A single vaporetto ticket costs around €9.50 (as of recent updates) and is valid for 75 minutes. Day passes, multi-day cards and the Rolling Venice Card offer better value for multiple rides. The tickets and prices guide covers current pricing in detail.

items.question: What is the difference between a vaporetto and a gondola?
items.answer: A vaporetto is Venice's public transport — a motorized waterbus carrying dozens of passengers on scheduled routes for the price of a bus ticket. A gondola is a traditional rowing boat for private hire, costing €80-100+ for a 30-minute ride. The comparison page covers all the differences.

items.question: Is vaporetto the best way to get around Venice?
items.answer: For most visitors, yes — the vaporetto is the most practical, affordable and scenic way to navigate Venice's historic centre and lagoon islands. The Line 1 route along the Grand Canal doubles as one of the world's great boat tours at bus-fare prices.
